items.title: The Stars Of Gucci's 2026 Holiday Dinner in Manila
items.summary: Gucci's annual Manila holiday dinner, held Nov 23 2026 at Uma Nota, brought together Filipino celebrities including Anne Curtis, Marian Rivera and James Reid wearing pieces from Core Cruise 2027 and Primavera Fall-Winter 2026. Coverage frames it as a warm, intimate gathering rather than a staged corporate event.

items.title: Gucci comes home - and lands in Manila
items.summary: Recap of Gucci's Manila holiday gathering unveiling the Cruise 2026 collection, which drew on the Palazzo Settimanni heritage and introduced the new Giglio bag. Attendees included Anne Curtis-Smith, Marian Rivera, James Reid and Kylie Verzosa. Coverage is strongly positive, framing the event as heritage-meets-modernity.

items.title: Gucci pays homage to Italian craftsmanship with its Cruise 2026 collection
items.summary: Manila Bulletin's writeup of the Gucci Cruise 2026 preview at Greenbelt 4, emphasizing Florentine craftsmanship themes and local celebrity attendance. Purely activation/PR coverage, no critical framing.

items.title: A starry, starry affair
items.summary: Society-page recap of the same Manila Gucci holiday gathering, listing attendees and outfits drawn from Gucci's Cruise 2026 and Core Cruise 2027 lines. Purely activation coverage.

items.title: Gucci Discount Strategy Puts Pressure On Luxury Rivals. Louis Vuitton Isn't Following
items.summary: Reports Gucci has cut prices on flagship items by up to 30% under CEO Luca de Meo (e.g. Padlock bag from EUR3,500 to EUR2,450) as middle-class luxury shoppers retreat, while Louis Vuitton's CFO rejects comparable discounting, saying 'we are not Coca-Cola.' Critical-angle: frames Gucci's move as breaking an industry pricing taboo amid weak demand.

items.title: Pasar Barang Mewah Lesu, Gucci dan Louis Vuitton Hadapi Dilema
items.summary: Indonesian-language piece on the three-year luxury slowdown: Gucci has posted 13 consecutive quarters of declining sales and has cut prices roughly 30% on some items (e.g. Padlock bag) under CEO Luca de Meo, while Louis Vuitton holds premium pricing. Critical-angle: frames Gucci's discounting as a sign of pressure from squeezed middle-class spenders.

items.title: Kering Q3 2026 shares sink as Gucci recovery lags
items.summary: Kering Q3 2026 revenue was EUR3,345m (-1% comparable); Gucci revenue fell 6% comparable to EUR1,291m, with Asia-Pacific down 8% in the quarter and 11% on a nine-month basis, plus 42 net store closures in APAC - the steepest regional contraction. Low mainland China traffic was cited as the main drag, pulling the broader Southeast Asia-inclusive APAC region down. Carried for regional earnings context though outside the strict 14-day window; included because it frames the demand backdrop cited in the Nov 16-17 critical pieces above.

items.title: NBI raid yields P42-M worth of fake Gucci products
items.summary: Philippine National Bureau of Investigation raid seized PHP42 million worth of counterfeit Gucci (and other luxury brand) goods in Manila. Critical/negative-adjacent angle: underscores the scale of Gucci counterfeiting pressure in the Philippine market, a chronic SEA-specific brand-protection issue.

items.title: A smart way to shop luxury (and avoid fakes)
items.summary: Consumer-guidance piece noting Gucci, Chanel and Louis Vuitton top authentication-request volumes in the Philippines, reflecting how counterfeiting remains a persistent drag on the brand's perceived exclusivity in the local market.

items.title: Da Nang store fined over $3,800 for selling fake Gucci, Chanel products
items.summary: Vietnamese authorities fined a Da Nang retailer for selling counterfeit Gucci and Chanel goods, part of a recurring enforcement pattern across Vietnam. Included as background on chronic counterfeit pressure in the Vietnam market despite being outside the 14-day freshness window; no more recent Vietnam-specific Gucci item surfaced today.

Fan/entertainment-press amplification of the same activation; engagement metrics not visible via public fetch (paywalled).
